title: Tristan & Yseult directed by Emma Rice at St. Ann’s Warehouse #trista...
transcript: This unique theatrical experience is closer to a Cirque du Soleil show than any play or musical. A story of forbidden love, presented in a retro nightclub with live music and mild absurdism, Tristan & Yseult is St Ann's latest production, though not its newest. The source material is a centuries-old myth, and this production, helmed by Emma Rice, originally premiered in 2003, though it has been at least somewhat updated for 2026 — I was not expecting to hear a Raye cover. It's pretty out there, but it won me over with its disarmingly irreverent humor, its musicianship, and most of all, its direction. It truly does feel like a Cirque du Soleil show in that the story is rendered in broad strokes, the characters are eccentric, and the direction is stunning. There is a plethora of absolutely gorgeous stage images and theatrical mechanisms used, to the point where perhaps fewer devices would actually give the show more narrative clarity. Yet, as a piece about love, one that's all-consuming in its passion and danger, some messiness feels appropriate — it's a fairy tale and a fever dream. Not every choice lands, but the batting average is quite high, and it's the kind of show where you can ascribe as much or as little meaning onto it as you want. I found it to be more thematically rich than it initially seemed, and would consider it a very memorable production.
